implementation_notes: In C the enclosing type is a file boundary rather than a class, so feature envy shows up as a function in one .c file whose body is mostly `other->field` reads. The remedy is the same move at file granularity: put the function next to the struct whose fields it touches and give it the right linkage, or make it `static` in that file. C has no privacy, so the envy is often accompanied by nothing stopping anyone else from doing the same computation — which is why an `inline` accessor set or a single exported function is the practical enforcement.
idiom_name: free function over a struct it does not belong to
pitfalls: `static` restricts linkage but not envy's reach; the function is still in the wrong file conceptually.
Because a header exposes every field, 'moving' is a convention only — a later caller will reach in again unless accessors become the only published API.
Function pointers in a vtable-like table make the envy structural: the table declares a dependency on every type it can compute over.
